audit_findings.title: The bridge mixes billions with millions
audit_findings.magnitude: $760.473 million equity-value overstatement, or $82.69 per share, computed from $854.833 million debt less $93.599 million cash versus the $0.761 million net deduction applied
audit_findings.mechanism: The unit error understates the net-debt deduction in the enterprise-to-equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We had long-term debt of $883 million at December 31, 2025 and $971 million at December 31, 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated mechanical error. Correcting only the units would reduce the reported bear, base, and bull values to approximately $298, $367, and $448 per share, respectively. The base value falls about 18%, and the 30%-margin buy-below level falls from $315 to approximately $257. It does not reverse the conclusion that $909.15 exceeds modeled value, but it materially changes every valuation output.
audit_findings.action: Convert cash to $93.599 million and debt to $854.833 million, verify the bridge formula, and rerun all scenarios and the buy-below calculation.

audit_findings.title: The historical numerator does not represent the current business perimeter
audit_findings.mechanism: The trend-based OE anchor largely reflects the legacy perimeter, whereas current shares and debt reflect AMPAC and Calca; full-period acquired-business OE, maintenance capital, amortization, taxes, and financing effects are absent from most historical observations.
audit_findings.evidence: We completed the acquisition of Calca on October 1, 2025 and the acquisition of AMPAC on January 16, 2024, both of which are part of the specialty materials segment.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, although its net valuation effect is not. AMPAC entered results on January 16, 2024 and Calca on October 1, 2025. Specialty materials produced $47.027 million of 2025 operating profit and $34.768 million in the first half of 2026, amounts large enough relative to the $294.6 million OE anchor to make the issue reasonably capable of materially changing value. Direction remains mixed because added operating cash flow may be offset by acquisition amortization, maintenance capital, taxes, and financing requirements.
audit_findings.action: Build same-perimeter or filed pro-forma OE for AMPAC and Calca, including full-year taxes, amortization adjustments, working capital, maintenance capital, and acquisition financing, then refit the anchor and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Debt may be deducted from an already levered earnings stream
audit_findings.magnitude: $854.833 million of debt, or approximately $92.95 per share, would be an improper additional deduction if OE is levered; 2025 filed interest and financing expense was $39.693 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Interest may already reduce a net-income- or operating-cash-flow-based OE numerator, while the enterprise-to-equity bridge subtracts the related debt principal again.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest and financing expenses were $40 million in 2025 and $57 million in 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved methodological possibility, not a demonstrated double count because the raw OE formula was not supplied. It becomes material when finding 1 is corrected: if OE is cash flow to equity, subtracting $854.833 million of debt would understate equity value by about $92.95 per share. Under the currently erroneous units, the actual debt subtraction is only about $0.09 per share, so the two findings must be resolved together without netting them away.
audit_findings.action: Trace each historical OE calculation to filed statement lines. If interest is retained, use an equity-cash-flow valuation with an equity required return and no debt deduction; otherwise remove financing effects, calculate unlevered after-tax cash flow, and retain the enterprise-value bridge.

audit_findings.title: Owner earnings may capitalize non-operating pension returns
audit_findings.magnitude: $53.029 million of 2025 pretax non-service pension and postretirement benefit income, computed from filed plan components; $29.353 million for the first half of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Non-service pension income may enter OE through reported earnings and then be capitalized as operating cash generation, although the associated restricted pension assets and plan obligations are not separately reconciled in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The amounts for both periods included the components of net periodic benefit cost (income), except for service costs, from defined benefit pension and postretirement plans, which also represent most of the difference between the two years.
audit_findings.explanation: The presence and scale of non-service pension income are demonstrated; its inclusion in the OE series remains unresolved without the raw formula. The 2025 amount equals about 18% of the $294.6 million anchor before considering tax-basis differences, so capitalization could materially overstate operating value. The company also reported a $605.366 million prepaid pension asset at June 30, 2026, meaning a proper separate pension reconciliation could offset part of the reduction, but the record does not establish how much is realizable by common owners.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct OE excluding non-service benefit income for every year, calculate the applicable tax adjustment, reconcile plan assets and projected obligations by plan, assess restrictions and expected contributions, and separately value only any realizable net pension position before rerunning the valuation.

audit_findings.title: The bridge may omit debt-like and legacy claims
audit_findings.mechanism: Incremental lease, benefit, environmental, asbestos, purchase, and other senior claims may require bridge deductions if their economic cost is not already captured in normalized OE.
audit_findings.evidence: These include debt-related obligations, lease obligations, purchase commitments, including those for property, plant, and equipment, contributions to pension and postretirement benefit plans, and environmental dismantling and decontamination.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate potentially relevant balances, including $85.097 million of operating-lease liabilities and $12 million of environmental accruals at June 30, 2026, plus $18.125 million of finance-lease liabilities at December 31, 2025. They do not establish which amounts are incremental to OE, which are already reflected through recurring expenses, or whether omitted assets and recoveries offset them. Materiality therefore cannot be determined from the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every June 2026 liability and commitment category to the OE formula; identify only obligations not already captured in normalized cash costs, net associated recoveries or assets, and rerun the bridge with the resulting incremental claims.

audit_findings.title: A disclosed one-time charge remains in the earnings history
audit_findings.mechanism: A genuinely nonrecurring cash charge depresses 2025 OE and may lower the fitted historical trend used as the valuation anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: The increased operating costs result primarily from lower production at our manufacturing plants and an increase in technology investments, as well as one-time charges related to our efforts to become more efficient by optimizing our global manufacturing network.
audit_findings.explanation: The existence of network-optimization charges is demonstrated, but neither their amount nor their cash character is disclosed in the supplied record. The filing also describes continuing manufacturing-network efficiency initiatives, so recurrence is unresolved. Because the anchor is a ten-year fitted trend of $294.6 million rather than the higher $399.3 million 2025 OE, the charge's effect on the anchor cannot be established without a refit and may be smaller than its effect on 2025 alone.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the charge amount and statement-of-cash-flow treatment, identify comparable charges in every historical year, determine whether optimization spending continues, apply a consistent normalization only to nonrecurring amounts, and refit the OE trend.
